_comment: klt erc supply spec for the merged top cell -- T1 checklist item 11
('Power delivery, structural', klayout-tools#2025/#2057) requires a
supply-net read of this shape for every block (issue #300). See
layout/README.md's 'Item 11' section for the full account of what this
run showed and does not show; this block only justifies each field.
Run it against the committed top-cell GDS:
klt erc layout/cells/temp_por_top.gds \
layout/cells/temp_por_top.erc-supply-spec.json --format json
producing layout/reports/temp_por_top/erc_supply.json.
Why each field is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at Poly2 rather than at Metal1. `active_layer` (Comp) makes
the gate-identification test `poly AND diff` instead of raw poly area,
which is what keeps this block's poly-resistor legs (temp_core's R2
ladder and bias_core's bias resistors -- real poly with no gate oxide)
out of `gates[]` (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area: poly n diff
vs. raw poly area', issue #1979). This block has no filler/filltie
masters (it is hand-drawn analog, not a placed-and-routed standard-cell
flow), but the same poly-without-oxide shape appears here as resistors.
- Metal1 through Metal5 is this block's full drawn interconnect stack
(layout/build_cells.py's own header comment: 'Nwell 21/0 . Comp 22/0 .
so the supply read has to cover every level a rail or a riser could be
drawn on, not just the levels the top-level VDD/VSS rails happen to use.
- `label_layer` is declared on Metal1 (34/10) and Metal2 (36/10), and
deliberately NOT on Metal3/Metal4/Metal5 -- verified against this
block's own merged GDS with `klt layers --flattened --include-text`
rather than assumed from another block's spec:
* 34/10 carries 48 text occurrences, including 5 VDD + 5 VSS --
layout/build_cells.py's per-sub-cell internal net labels (each
sub-cell's own VDD/VSS pin, dropped on its own Metal1 riser; see
METAL1_LABEL, e.g. the bias_core/por_comparator/por_output_chain/
temp_core instances' own `b.label("VDD", ...)` / `b.label("VSS",
...)` calls).
* 36/10 carries 5 text occurrences: CTAT, PTAT, RESETn, VDD, VSS --
this is `_top_cell`'s own METAL2_LABEL set, i.e. the block's
RATIFIED 5-PAD PINOUT (layout/build_cells.py: 'the ratified 5-pad
pinout ... VDD/VSS are labelled on their rails ... the *only*
labels drawn directly in this cell'). This is the label set
`top_cell_pins` (klayout-tools#291) turns into the chip's own pin
list.
* Metal3 (42/0), Metal4 (46/0) and Metal5 (81/0) carry NO text at
all in this GDS (`text_count: 0` for every layer/datatype pair on
those levels) -- Metal5 in particular is drawn only as the MiM
capacitor plates' Via4 escape route in bias_core and
por_output_chain (layout/build_cells.py: 'Via3 40/0 . Via4 41/0 .
Metal5 81/0 (the drawn MiM units' plate routing, #264 -- ... the
top plate's only escape is Via4 -> Metal5 -> a second Via4 down a
fresh Metal4 island, both cells only)'), never a supply rail. This
is the opposite of the fleet's own digital-flow worked example
(gf180-drone-fc's layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json labels
Metal1 and Metal5, because its PDN's top strap is on Metal5) --
the label_layer choice tracks what a block's own GDS actually
carries pin text on, not a fixed per-PDK convention.
- GDS layer numbers cross-checked two ways, per issue #300: against
layout/build_cells.py's own layer constants (already the numbers klt's
curated gf180mcu deck reads, per layout/README.md), AND independently
against the installed PDK's own tech file
(libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp): Poly2 30/0, COMP 22/0, Metal1
34/0, Metal1_Label 34/10, Metal2 36/0, Metal2_Label 36/10, Metal3 42/0,
Metal4 46/0, Metal5 81/0, Contact 33/0, Via1 35/0, Via2 38/0, Via3
40/0, Via4 41/0 -- every one of the 15 <source> entries matched
exactly.
- `vias[]` bridges every adjacent stackup pair with this PDK's own
contact/via layer, so a supply riser that only makes electrical sense
through a via (e.g. a Metal1 rail reached from a Metal2 label) is not
reported as disconnected purely because `klt erc`'s connectivity model
was never told the via exists.
- `nets[]`: VDD and VSS both `kind: "supply"`, which is what makes a
short between them report as the severe `erc.supply_short` rather than
the general `erc.multiply_driven_net`. Each must resolve to exactly
ONE electrical island: `erc.unconnected_net` fires on zero matches
(nothing in the layout carries that label at all) AND on more than one
(the rail is split into pieces that never touch) -- so ZERO findings of
that rule is exactly the 'one island per supply' verdict, not merely an
absence of a report.
- `devices[]` declares this block's drawn poly-resistor bodies so the
connectivity model stops reading them as wires (klayout-tools#2183,
fixed by klayout-tools#2205 at commit ddf47e78). `klt erc` traces
wire/via connectivity only -- it registers no device extraction -- so
without this declaration every drawn resistor body conducts across its
own extent, and a supply-sensing resistive divider across the rails (the
defining topology of a power-on-reset comparator, which this block is)
reports a FALSE `erc.supply_short` no matter how clean the layout is.
That is exactly what the first committed run of this spec showed; see
layout/README.md's 'Item 11' section for that history.
- `body_layer` is RES_MK (110/5), NOT the `Resistor` high-sheet-rho ID
layer (62/0), and the difference matters. 62/0 is only the *class*
selector that picks `ppolyf_u_1k` out of the resistor family: in this
GDS it is drawn on 251 shapes, all of them in `bias_core` (24) and
`por_comparator` (227), and NONE in `temp_core` -- whose R2 gain-ladder
segments are plain `ppolyf_u` bodies (layout/build_cells.py's
`_r_segment` draws PPLUS/SAB/RES_MK and no 62/0). RES_MK is the deck's
resistor-*candidate* marker, required for every recognised flavour, and
is drawn on all 301 body shapes (bias_core 24 + por_comparator 227 +
temp_core 50). Measured on this GDS: RES_MK n Poly2 = 50526.34 um2
versus Resistor(62/0) n Poly2 = 41858.34 um2 -- declaring 62/0 alone
would leave 8668.00 um2 of real resistor body still modelled as wire.
Both clear the false `erc.supply_short`; only RES_MK describes the
layout completely, so RES_MK is what is declared.
- Over-coverage cross-check, per `klt erc`'s own warning that the
subtraction is purely geometric ('it cuts, so declare it where the
device is'): RES_MK n (Poly2 n Comp) = 0.000 um2, i.e. the carve-out
removes no gate region at all, and the run reports zero
`erc.unconnected_net` and zero `erc.floating_gate`. Note that
`provenance.devices[0].body_area_um2` reads 53126.74, which is RES_MK's
own merged area rather than the 50526.34 um2 actually subtracted from
Poly2 -- the 2600.40 um2 difference is `_r_segment`'s deliberate
+/-0.3 um marker overhang in x, which sits over no conductor and so
subtracts nothing. That the field reports the marker area rather than
the subtracted area is an upstream reporting gap, filed generically as
klayout-tools#2226; it does not affect this run's verdict, but it is
why the area cross-check above was measured independently rather than
read out of the report.
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and that is a recorded
gap rather than an oversight. Declaring one on a real routed layout
collapses the whole design into one electrical island and reports a
FALSE `erc.supply_short` -- upstream bug klayout-tools#2169, reproduced
four ways in gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION.md F-034 on that repo's own
digital flow. This block was not independently re-tested against the
same collapse (doing so would require declaring the very ties[] this
spec omits), but the bug report is general (`klt erc`'s ties[]
matching, not this PDK or this block), so the same avoidance applies
here. Because `ties[]` is omitted, `erc.missing_tie` is NOT COMPUTED by
this run (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely ->
erc.missing_tie is never computed') -- its absence from the committed
report's `erc_findings` is an absence of evidence, not evidence of
absence. layout/README.md's 'Item 11' section names what well-tie
evidence stands in for it instead.
